payload.summary: All six amendments identify real, verified issues in the codebase. The exploration confirmed: (1) concentration helpers redundantly recompute water_volume_l() ~11 times per snapshot, (2) nitrifier yields were increased ~50x alongside the helper refactor, (3) Monod kinetics use total-mass parameterization with doc comments that could mislead, (4) soft_acidic.toml values were doubled without documented rationale, (5) core biological rate code still uses raw totals not concentration helpers, and (6) save.rs hard-rejects schema 2 with no migration path despite existing infrastructure to support one. Each amendment is technically sound and actionable.

votes.rationale: Verified: every concentration helper (11+ in snapshot.rs::from_state) independently calls water_volume_l() which calls substrate_depth_cm() iterating all substrate layers. The volume is invariant within a single tick so this is pure waste. The fix is trivial — compute volume once and pass it or cache it. Low severity but zero-risk improvement, and the pattern will get worse as more helpers are added.

Verified: AOB yield is 0.05, NOB 0.04, comammox 0.03, plus a hardcoded 0.5g logistic carrying capacity in nitrogen_cycle.rs:246. These are massive behavioral changes to cycling dynamics — a 50x yield increase means biofilter maturation is dramatically faster. Bundling these with a structural refactor (concentration helpers) makes it impossible to isolate regressions from intentional behavioral changes. These should be separate, independently revertable changesets with explicit justification for the new parameter values.

Verified: ProcessParams doc comments say things like 'Half-saturation for TAN (mg N total)' and 'Half-saturation for DO (mg total)'. While technically accurate, Monod K_s is physically a concentration quantity — the same total-mass K_s produces different effective concentrations in different tank volumes. Since concentration-based kinetics are deferred to tanksim-6e5.2.3, adding a one-line note like 'Interim total-mass parameterization; will be converted to concentration-based in tanksim-6e5.2.3' is near-zero cost and prevents misinterpretation by future contributors.

Verified: soft_acidic.toml has alkalinity=1.07 meq/L, DIC=12.0 mg/L, bicarbonate=65.3 mg/L — all exactly doubled from the reported previous values. The new values do yield ~3 dKH which is reasonable for 'soft acidic' water, but the doubling pattern strongly suggests compensation for a volume-basis change rather than an independent correction. Without documented rationale, it's impossible to verify whether this was intentional and correct. Undocumented data changes bundled with structural refactors are a maintenance hazard.

Verified and this is the most critical issue. nitrogen_cycle.rs:76-78 extracts raw doc_total/don_total/do_total for decomposer limitation. algae_growth.rs:32-38 uses raw ammonia_total_mg_n_total + nitrate_mg_n_total. plant_growth.rs:23,36-37 uses raw dic_mg_c_total and N/P totals. All Monod/half-saturation computations operate on mass totals, meaning two tanks with identical concentrations but different volumes will produce different biological rates. The concentration helper layer is purely cosmetic until it's wired into the actual kinetics. This is a physical correctness defect that undermines the stated purpose of the refactor.

Verified: save.rs:43-47 hard-rejects any schema != 3 with SimError::SchemaVersionMismatch. No migration path exists. Meanwhile, WaterState::rescale_totals_for_volume (water.rs:179-202) already scales all 17 total-mass fields by a volume ratio, and geometry helpers can compute both old gross and new net volumes. A schema 2→3 migration is feasible with existing infrastructure: load schema 2, compute old gross volume, compute new net volume, call rescale_totals_for_volume, bump schema version. Permanently breaking every existing save for a units refactor — when migration tools already exist — is an unnecessarily destructive user-facing regression.
